title: Training-Free Evidence-Grounded Visual Reasoning for Open-Vocabulary Object Detection in Remote Sensing
content: Open-Vocabulary Object Detection (OVOD) in Remote Sensing (RS) aims to detect arbitrary objects from overhead perspective with complex scenes. Although most existing methods leverage large-scale vision-language pre-training, fine-tuning, or semi-supervised learning to form a region-text alignment ability for OVOD, the ambiguous or similar appearances of isolated objects in RS scenes often lead to semantic misalignment due to the absence of context understanding. To address this issue, a novel Training-Free evidence-grounded Gauss-What Visual Reasoning, called TF-GVR, is proposed for OVOD in RS, which reformulates OVOD as a visual reasoning task that integrates visual evidence for identifying unknown objects. First, pre-trained class-agnostic region proposal networks are combined to retain potential foreground proposals, serving as visual anchors for the subsequent visual reasoning. Then, for each visual anchor, a multi-scale visual search protocol collaborates pre-trained visual language model to collect contextual visual evidence, mapping searched visual slices to diverse text snippets via a one-to-many region-text soft-alignment. Finally, a zero-shot visual chain-of-thought prompt is designed to explicitly deduce over the gathered text snippets and spatial relations by capitalizing on the logical reasoning ability of pre-trained large language models. To verify the effectiveness, extensive experiments on the DIOR and NWPUVHR-10 datasets demonstrate that our training-free framework, built exclusively upon off-the-shelf foundation models, achieves superior OVOD performance compared to advanced methods, alongside enhanced interpretability and traceability.
